digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow — macOS pytest execution
propositions: RAM-disk storage placement for macOS pytest temporary trees was hypothesized to reduce Gerrit Verify critical-path runtime by avoiding small-write latency, following precedent from Apple Git CI and Aeron.

Four independent treatment runs (31869753711, 31869919362, 31870391571, 31873067707) all executed slower than the exact no-RAM control (31868300174: 17m26s default / 20m36s job), with treatment timings ranging 18m26s–20m54s, failing the predeclared 5% improvement threshold of ≤16m33.7s default / ≤19m34.2s job.

The first treatment exposed a cleanup defect: intentionally owner-nonwritable workflow snapshot fixtures made recursive basetemp removal raise PermissionError; recursive observability added 71–98 seconds of runner occupancy.

Patchset 3 exposed a nested-pytest cacheprovider leak that caused false test collection skew in Ubuntu jobs; exact reproduction confirmed the defect and verified the fix (adding -p no:cacheprovider to the nested process).

The experiment was rejected per AC7 retention oracle; merged change 1806 removed the RAM-disk lifecycle and restored both unchanged pytest tiers to runner.temp, keeping selectors, markers, workers, timeouts, platforms, coverage, and assertions identical.

Final successful run 31873067707 on the restored no-RAM path passed all four full suites and hosted macOS cleanup without device leaks, confirming the reversion was safe; parent runtime and import-latency tracking remain open.
